reviews.review: A solid 7/10 corridor pve shooter that is a ton of fun to play and does a great job of incorporating melee and promoting variety in weaponry. This was my introduction into the sci fi Warhammer 40k universe, and it was an immersive blast. Titus and the Ultramarines, the protagonists, look like a bunch of classic meatheads, but are actually cool, thoughtful, and interesting characters. Much of the game is standard shooter stuff, running around using whatever is at hand to gun down waves of Orks as you try to retake an invaded world. The weapon and ability progression is great, allowing you to choose whether to use a classic assault rifle, a variety of energy weapons, grenade launchers and plasma shotguns and providing weapon caches often enough so you can pick and choose what to use each fight. The game also suits melee combat very well, allowing for charging in headfirst with a giant axe, popping a fury to smash through a horde, swapping to a bolter to snipe some long range Orks, and ducking into cover while waiting for your shield to recharge. Even if you get caught out, the ability heal with melee finishers means you will always have a place in a fight. It all culminates with a fun boss fight about 75% of the way, but unfortunately the end of the game is a bit of a mess. The nature of the end game enemies eliminates a lot of weapon options, especially melee outside of spot duty, resulting in a slog through the final chapters and limping into a QTE final boss. Storywise, it is a fun romp, about on par with your average Gears of Wars, Bulletstorms, Uncharted 1s of the same general era of shoot stuff first and add story later. If you want a nice fun palate cleanser game to take up 8 hours of your life, this one is a ton of fun, although the closing chapters may leave a bad taste in your mouth.

VERDICT:
I've never been into the tabletop version but put into a game and focusing on one particular person, it's a whole different ball game and 10x more fun! The story was good and the gameplay was brilliant, even though this game is 10 years old, I still got as much fun out of it if it was a new game. The only downfall I saw was the online play, sadly that is dead and only comes to life if it's organised.
Total Score = 63/100.

GAMEPLAY:
In Space Marine, the player engages enemies with both melee and ranged from a third-person point of view. The player character, Titus, has regenerative abilities. When his health gets low, performing some actions can allow Titus to regain a portion of his health. Titus is accompanied by the characters Sidonus and Leandros for most of the missions, though some missions are performed alone. The game features a fury meter that, when filled up, allows the player to either slow time for aiming or perform powerful melee attacks.

The starting weapons include a combat knife and a pistol, though the player can acquire other weapons. The game also includes a new weapon not featured in the table-top game known as the Vengeance Launcher, which can shoot sticky grenades.

The game's main antagonists are the Orks and the Forces of Chaos. The Orks are an alien race of brutish warriors. The Forces of Chaos are an even greater threat, and can summon monsters that live in a parallel dimension known as The Warp. Portals conjured by the Traitor Legions allow daemons to enter the battlefield.

■■■■■■□□□□ 6 / 10

There needs to be more games like this.
